newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS ENDS DIFFICULT YEAR WITH DRAMATIC WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS ENDS DIFFICULT YEAR WITH DRAMATIC WIN.

text.p: Pete Sampras will take a long time to cast the sad memories of this year's death of his coach and close friend Tim Gullikson from the forefront of his mind.

After playing one of the most dramatic five-set matches of his career against Boris Becker to win the ATP world championship on Sunday, the American was soon talking about the loss of one of the most important men in his life.
"This year, especially off the court, has been very difficult," the world number one said. "Tim would want me to keep on playing hard and playing well and continuing to be happy.
"And when you play matches like this it reminds you of the things he told you. It still hurts but we have, just have, to move on."
Sampras and Becker both described the four-hour final as one of their best matches. It ended 3-6 7-6 7-6 6-7 6-4 in the American's favour.

It is a measure of the maturity of Sampras that, despite a year of personal tragedy, he managed to produce such a brilliant performance against an inspired Becker in front of 15,000 fervent German fans.

Sampras will keep his place at the top of the game when the final world rankings for the year are published on Monday and has now won the season-ending championship three times, equalling the records of Becker and John McEnroe.
Only Ivan Lendl (in the 1980s) and Ilie Nastase (in the 1970s) have won more. Sampras also won the event, which used to be known as the Masters, in 1991 and 1994.

The U.S. Open champion joins Jimmy Connors and McEnroe as the only player to have finished at the top of the sport for four consecutive years. Sampras has held the prestigious position at the end of every season since 1993.
Becker believes Sampras belongs to the all-time greats.
"I said a few years ago that, if that guy keeps playing the way he has been, he has a chance of being the greatest ever," the triple Wimbledon champion said.

"I have played with the likes of Lendl or McEnroe or Conners. I even practised with (Bjorn) Borg and there is absolutely no comparison. If I would play right now how I did 10 years ago, I would have no chance against Pete."
